function: Radar multi-target detection and per-target analog beam-index prediction from range-angle radar images, feeding target-to-user association by the Hungarian algorithm (pp. 7-8).
system: Downlink hybrid sub-connected mmWave MIMO BS (planar array 2x2 to 64x64) serving vehicles with 2x2 arrays, co-located 128x4 FMCW radar, 28 GHz, no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: YOLOv8s convolutional detector with added beam-index classification outputs; supervised training on simulated radar images, 5-fold cross-validation; non-learned Hungarian assignment on a BCE-loss cost matrix (pp. 8, 10).
data_channel: Custom ray tracing: Remcom Wireless InSite (communication) and WaveFarer (radar) on OpenStreetMap urban maps with SUMO traffic, three scenarios; same simulated data for training and testing (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Trained at -10 dB SNR per antenna, tested from -55 to -10 dB; 5-fold cross-validation averaged over three scenarios; no unseen scenario or site (pp. 9-10).
baselines: Learned detectors only: Faster R-CNN (ResNet101-FPN) and SSD (VGG16) versus YOLOv8s on scenario C radar target detection; no non-learned baseline, none for beam prediction or association (p. 11).
metrics: Precision, recall, F1, mAP50, mAP50-95 for targets and beams (Table II); beam top-k accuracy (Fig. 8); probability of correct association (Figs. 9-11) (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Parameter counts reported: about 11.2M for YOLOv8s, 60.7M Faster R-CNN, 24.7M SSD; no FLOPs or runtime, only a qualitative efficiency claim (p. 12).
openness: none (YOLOv8 and MMDetection are third-party libraries; no link to the authors' code or simulated data) (p. 15).
q1_support: p. 9: "has been simulated using Remcom Wireless InSite". Custom ray tracing on OpenStreetMap scenarios built by the authors; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO dataset, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "trained over analog precoding beam indices determined at -10 dB SNR per antenna, while the performance of the model is examined over all the considered communication SNRs range". SNR sweep only; p. 10 uses 5-fold cross-validation on the same data; no unseen scenario, band, or adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "Faster R-CNN [18] and SSD [14], over the radar vehicular target detection". Only learned detectors are compared, for radar target detection; no non-learned baseline, and no baseline for beam prediction or association.
q4_support: p. 12: "11.2 · 106 model parameters for YOLOv8s". That is 10^6, about 11.2 million parameters, against 60.7 million for Faster R-CNN and 24.7 million for SSD; no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 9: "has been simulated using Remcom Wireless InSite". Data are simulated by the authors and not public; no link to their code or data, and the only link (p. 15) is the third-party YOLOv8 library.
notes: Borderline scope: the learned YOLOv8 jointly detects radar targets and predicts analog beam indices (communication-centric ISAC), whereas the target-to-user association is a Hungarian assignment (p. 8). Included as area 5 (ISAC beams), not above_phy, because a physical-layer beam decision is learned. q1 is 0 because the ray tracing is the authors' own Wireless InSite scenarios, not DeepMIMO; reviewer to confirm. q4 counts the parameter count of YOLOv8s.
